plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-panel diagram of a right triangle drawn in the complex plane, with the horizontal axis labeled "Real" and the vertical axis labeled "Imaginary," each drawn as a thin double-headed arrow through the origin. A filled black dot sits in the first quadrant and is labeled "x + yi." A straight segment runs from the origin out to that dot and is labeled r; from the dot a vertical segment drops to the horizontal axis and is labeled y, and the horizontal leg from the origin to the foot of that drop is labeled x, closing the triangle with a right angle at the foot. The angle at the origin, between the positive real direction and the segment r, is marked with a small arc and labeled with the Greek letter theta. A heavier curved arc of constant radius sweeps through the labeled dot and carries arrowheads at both ends, one pointing left beyond the imaginary axis and the other pointing down beyond the real axis, tracing a circle centered at the origin. Laying the rectangular pair x and y and the polar pair r and theta on the same picture lets the reader read either description off the other. The drawing fixes r as the modulus, the distance from the origin to the point, and theta as the direction angle, the two quantities that make up the polar form of a complex number.

interactionPlan.concept: A complex number x + yi can be located either by its rectangular coordinates (x, y) or by its polar pair (r, θ), and the right triangle in the complex plane converts between them: x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ, r = √(x²+y²).
elements: Horizontal double-headed thin arrow through the origin labeled 'Real' at its right end
Vertical double-headed thin arrow through the origin labeled 'Imaginary' at its top
Origin point at the intersection of the two axes
Filled dark dot in the first quadrant representing the complex number
Label 'x + yi' in dark blue placed just above-right of the dot
Straight dark-blue segment from the origin to the dot (the hypotenuse), labeled 'r' at its midpoint, offset to the upper-left
Vertical dark-blue segment dropping from the dot to the real axis, labeled 'y' to its right
Horizontal dark-blue segment from the origin to the foot of the vertical drop, labeled 'x' below it
Small right-angle square marker at the foot of the vertical drop
Small arc at the origin between the positive real axis and the hypotenuse, labeled 'θ'

Heavy dark-blue circular arc of radius r centered at the origin, passing through the dot, with arrowheads at both ends (one sweeping left past the imaginary axis, one sweeping down past the real axis)
Optional readout panel showing current values of x, y, r, θ and the two forms 'x + yi' and 'r(cos θ + i sin θ)'

interactions.label: Direction angle θ (degrees)
interactions.teaches: Rotating the point along a fixed circle changes x and y together while r stays constant — θ controls direction only, and the legs shrink/grow and change sign as the point crosses quadrants.

interactions.label: Modulus r
interactions.teaches: r is literally the distance from the origin to the point: increasing it scales the circle, the hypotenuse, and both legs proportionally without changing the direction.

interactions.label: Annotation style
interactions.teaches: The same fixed point carries two equivalent descriptions; swapping the labels shows that x + yi and r(cos θ + i sin θ) name one location, not two.

demo_steps.title: The point and its triangle
demo_steps.narration: A complex number x + yi is plotted as a point in the plane, with the real part measured along the horizontal axis and the imaginary part along the vertical axis. Dropping a perpendicular to the real axis forms a right triangle whose legs are exactly x and y.

demo_steps.title: Naming the hypotenuse and the angle
demo_steps.narration: The hypotenuse from the origin is the modulus r, and the angle it makes with the positive real axis is θ. These two numbers locate the point just as completely as x and y do.

demo_steps.title: Sweep θ around the circle
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ and the point rides the heavy circular arc: r never changes, but x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ stretch, shrink, and change sign as the point moves through each quadrant.

demo_steps.title: Change r, keep the direction
demo_steps.narration: Now hold θ fixed and grow r. The circle and the hypotenuse expand together and both legs scale by the same factor — r really is distance from the origin, not an extra label.

demo_steps.title: Two names, one point
demo_steps.narration: Switch the annotations back and forth: the dot never moves, yet it reads as x + yi in rectangular form and r(cos θ + i sin θ) in polar form. The triangle is the dictionary between them.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: r and θ are not new information — they are the hypotenuse and base angle of the very triangle whose legs are x and y, so trigonometry translates directly between x + yi and r(cos θ + i sin θ).
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: White background, single panel. Thin black double-headed arrows form the axes through a centered origin (origin sits slightly left-of-center and low, so the first quadrant dominates). Axis labels 'Real' (right, italic bold) and 'Imaginary' (top, italic bold). All construction lines — hypotenuse, vertical leg, horizontal leg, and the heavy circular arc — in a dark navy blue; the arc is noticeably thicker than the triangle edges and carries arrowheads at both ends so it reads as a full circle being traced. The point is a solid black/navy dot with the label 'x + yi' in navy just above-right. Labels 'r' sits along the hypotenuse offset up-left, 'y' to the right of the vertical leg, 'x' below the horizontal leg, and 'θ' just inside a small arc at the origin. Include a faint right-angle marker where the vertical leg meets the real axis. When sliders move, the dot, triangle legs, angle arc, and circle radius all update live; a small text readout near a corner shows x, y, r, θ and both algebraic forms. Labels fade in/out according to the toggle rather than the geometry changing.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for theta: the learner drags the angle from the positive real axis, the point moves around the circular arc while x and y legs update, and the link between direction angle and rectangular coordinates becomes clear.
- Slider for r: the learner changes the modulus, the segment from the origin and the circle radius grow or shrink with the point, and r becomes visible as distance from the origin rather than a separate label.
- Toggle between rectangular and polar labels: the learner switches the displayed annotations from x and y to r and theta, the same point keeps its position while the labels change, and the equivalence between x + yi and polar form is emphasized.

authoredContext:
We review these relationships in the figure.

Triangle plotted in the complex plane (x axis is real, y axis is imaginary). Base is along the x/real axis, height is some y/imaginary value in Q 1, and hypotenuse r extends from origin to that point (x+yi) in Q 1. The angle at the origin is theta. There is an arc going through (x+yi).

We use the term modulus to represent the absolute value of a complex number, or the distance from the origin to the point (x,y). The modulus, then, is the same as r, the radius in polar form. We use θ to indicate the angle of direction (just as with polar coordinates). Substituting, we have

discrepancies: Default (step-0) state uses the 'Rectangular (x, y)' annotation mode, which fades the polar group to 0.45 opacity — the heavy navy arc, the hypotenuse and the 'r' label render as pale grey instead of the bold navy of the source, so the default view does not read as a drop-in replacement for the static figure.
A white readout panel (x, y, r, θ, rectangular/polar forms) sits in the upper-right of the drawing area; nothing like it exists in the source and it competes visually with the figure.
A small right-angle square marker at the foot of the perpendicular and a black dot at the origin are added; neither appears in the source.
The 'x + yi' label is placed up-and-left of the dot (pushed by the radial offset/clamp), whereas the source places it to the upper-right of the dot, close beside it.

The heavy arc in the source clearly crosses the imaginary axis and terminates well below the real axis with a downward arrow; the generated arc sweep (θ−75° to θ+58°) ends nearer the axes, making the arc noticeably shorter/less dramatic.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful complex-plane triangle with excellent, pedagogically meaningful interaction (two sliders, annotation-mode select, 5-step narrated demo, tooltips/popups), but the default step dims the arc/hypotenuse/r to pale grey and adds an unrequested readout panel, so the at-a-glance match to the source is weakened.
action_items: Make the default (step 1) state use the 'Both' annotation mode, or keep polar opacity at 1.0 at start, so the heavy navy arc, hypotenuse and 'r' label match the source's full-strength navy.
Move the numeric readout out of the drawing canvas into the side UI panel (or hide it by default) so the figure area matches the source composition.

Place the 'x + yi' label just up-and-right of the dot as in the source instead of along the radial direction, and drop the origin dot / right-angle square (or make them subtle) to avoid elements absent from the original.
Extend the arc sweep so it visibly crosses the imaginary axis on the left and ends below the real axis on the right, matching the source's quarter-plus arc with both arrowheads.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are sound (no plan action items); the issues are concrete rendering fixes — default opacity/mode, removing the in-canvas readout and extra markers, label placement, and arc sweep extent.
